full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Priya Mondal. During his possession, he died leaving 2 minor sons namely, Pagla Mondal and Lalit Mondal. One Haribala Mondal, uncle of Pagla Mondal and Lalit Mondal, settled 22 areas of land with Sreemanta Mistry by registered patta dated 12-4-1928, Haribala Mondal again settled 1.75 acres of land by registered patta dated 5-4-1928 in favour of Sreemanta Mondal. One Krishna Mondal also settled 2.50 acres of land in favour of Sreemanta Mistry and In this way Sreemanta Mistry acquired total 5.37 acres of land, During his possession, he died leaving three sons, namely, Saradakanta Mistry, Barada Kanta Mistry and Aswani Mistry. There was dispute among the co-sharers and plaintiff No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 218 of 1951 for partition and declaration of title and the suit was decreed on compromise on 7-9-1958. Through Advocate Commissioner, the plaintiffs of that suit got possession of5.36 acres instead of 5.37 acres of land. Barada Kanta Mistry died leaving two sons, plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 and Aswani Mistry died leaving 3 sons, plaintiff Nos. 4-6. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land but the SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in' the name of defendant Nos. 3, 5, 6 and father of defendant No. 4, namely, Kritiram Mandai, The defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. Defendant Nos. 1-3 most illegally included the suit land in the list of vested and non-resident property and the same was illegally leased out to defendant Nos. 7-10. The cause of action arose on 15th of Magh, 1384 BS. When defendant Nos. 1-3 and 7-10 threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the suit land. For the reasons stated, the plaintiffs filed the suit.
